records.title: Retention mail now uses the one mailer, and logins with no SMTP are refused openly. Sender-domain authentication (SES identity, DKIM, SPF, DMARC) is still unmanaged, the default sender is .pro, and a dead second mailer remains
records.evidenceAtHead: FIXED PARTS: server/jobs/retentionCron.ts:288-332 notifyAdmins now calls sendGenericEmail (server/services/emailService.ts:396), which reads SMTP_HOST/SMTP_USER/SMTP_PASS. It no longer reads SMTP_PASSWORD/EMAIL_FROM, and an undelivered summary raises retention_notify_failed. `npx vitest run server/jobs/__tests__/retentionCron.policies.test.ts` passes 13/13; its test at :103/:265 plants a decoy SMTP_PASSWORD. server/services/email/smtp-config.ts:25 is now the only isEmailConfigured predicate. server/services/auth/login-code-delivery.ts:54 canDeliverLoginCode() is used at routes/auth.ts:682 and :2007 and at routes/authEnterprise.ts:421, so in production a login with no SMTP gets AUTH_OTP_UNDELIVERABLE instead of a false 'code sent'. STILL OPEN: (a) `grep -rniE 'aws_ses|dkim|dmarc|spf|route53' terraform/` finds nothing. Terraform only takes a free-text var smtp_from (terraform/stack/variables.tf:292-299, unchanged since 92ccdba1) and renders it at terraform/stack/main.tf:288. SPF/DKIM/DMARC appears only as a manual checklist line in scripts/ops/verify-otp-delivery.mjs:239,585,604. (b) emailService.ts:40 still has `process.env.SMTP_FROM || 'noreply@concept2cure.pro'`, while links and support in the same file use concept2cure.com (:102-106, :243, :253-255, :303). (c) server/services/notify.ts:1-15 still builds its own nodemailer transport with MAIL_FROM defaulting to 'no-reply@yourapp.local'. It has no callers; `grep -rn notifyOverride` finds only notify.ts:17 and the re-export at server/services/index.ts:77. (d) The boot check at server/startup/services.ts:284-303 only console.error()s when SMTP is unset. It never checks the sender domain, and readiness (server/startup/readiness-state.ts, inline-endpoints.ts) ignores email. (e) No CI gate limits createTransport to one module; `grep createTransport scripts/ci .github` finds nothing.
records.fixedBy: 177a0a00f: retention summary goes through sendGenericEmail (server/jobs/retentionCron.ts:288-332). 31a4aace7: one SMTP predicate (server/services/email/smtp-config.ts:25), and logins refused when a code can't be delivered (server/services/auth/login-code-delivery.ts:54; server/routes/auth.ts:682,2007; server/routes/authEnterprise.ts:421).
records.remaining: 1) The sending domain is not authenticated as code: no SES identity, DKIM, SPF or DMARC in Terraform, and nothing ties smtp_from to a verified domain, so pharma mail gateways can quarantine the login OTP. 2) The silent default sender 'noreply@concept2cure.pro' (emailService.ts:40) conflicts with the .com links and the .com support address in the same templates. 3) A second, dead mail transport remains in server/services/notify.ts, and no CI gate stops a third. 4) Boot and readiness never check that SMTP_FROM's domain is verified; the only check is a log line. 5) Whether real mail reaches a customer inbox can only be settled operationally: run scripts/ops/verify-otp-delivery.mjs against the target environment and read the Authentication-Results headers.
records.severityRationale: Login OTP is the mandatory second factor, so if a pilot customer's mail gateway quarantines mail from an unauthenticated domain, nobody at that customer can log in (a Sev-1 under SUPPORT_POLICY.md). The code no longer lies when SMTP is absent, which removes the silent failure, but deliverability still depends on manual DNS and SES work that the repo neither declares nor checks. The founder can verify it by hand before the pilot starts, so this is P1, not P0.
records.humanTestingNote: Applies only to deployed or staging environments with NODE_ENV=production. Locally (NODE_ENV!=production) the code is written to the server debug log. Symptom 1: with SMTP unset, login stops after the password with 'We could not send your verification code, so sign-in cannot be completed. This is a problem with the server…' (AUTH_OTP_UNDELIVERABLE). Symptom 2: with SMTP set but an unauthenticated SMTP_FROM domain (the default is noreply@concept2cure.pro), the code goes to spam or is quarantined by corporate gateways, and the tester waits on the code screen. Workaround: before the test session, run `node scripts/ops/verify-otp-delivery.mjs` against the staging environment with each tester's real inbox. Set SMTP_FROM to an address on a domain that is verified with the SMTP provider and has SPF/DKIM/DMARC. Have testers check spam. Personal Gmail inboxes are more forgiving than corporate M365 gateways.
records.instructions: 1. Founder: pick the single product domain (.com, .pro, .ai or trialsage.ai, an open question in the audit) and the sending subdomain (e.g. mail.<domain>). Make sure the AWS account's SES is out of the sandbox in us-east-1. 2. Terraform: create terraform/modules/ses-identity with aws_sesv2_email_identity (domain identity, Easy DKIM RSA_2048_BIT) and aws_sesv2_email_identity_mail_from_attributes (MAIL FROM subdomain, behavior_on_mx_failure = "REJECT_MESSAGE"). Output the three DKIM CNAME records, the MAIL FROM MX record, the SPF TXT record ("v=spf1 include:amazonses.com -all") and a DMARC TXT record ("v=DMARC1; p=quarantine; rua=mailto:dmarc@<domain>"). If the zone is in Route 53, add aws_route53_record resources gated on a new optional var dns_zone_id; otherwise surface them in terraform/stack/outputs.tf for the registrar. Instantiate the module from terraform/stack/main.tf. Add var mail_domain to terraform/stack/variables.tf, and add a validation on smtp_from (variables.tf:292-299) that its domain equals var.mail_domain or ends with "." + var.mail_domain. Add a run to terraform/stack/tests/boot_contract.tftest.hcl with expect_failures = [var.smtp_from] for a mismatched domain, and show it failing before adding the validation. 3. server/services/emailService.ts:40: remove the 'noreply@concept2cure.pro' fallback. In server/services/email/smtp-config.ts:25, make isEmailConfigured() also require SMTP_FROM when NODE_ENV==='production'. Signup (routes/auth.ts:933-940) and login (login-code-delivery.ts:54) then refuse honestly instead of sending from an unverified default. Extend server/services/auth/__tests__/login-code-delivery.test.ts with the case SMTP_HOST/USER/PASS set and SMTP_FROM unset in production, expecting canDeliverLoginCode()===false. It must fail at HEAD first. 4. Replace the hard-coded 'https://concept2cure.com' fallbacks at emailService.ts:102-106, :253-255 and :303 with the deployment origin (APP_URL, the same source resolveAppBaseUrl uses in routes/auth.ts). Replace 'support@concept2cure.com' at :243 with process.env.SUPPORT_EMAIL, and omit the sentence when it is unset (see GTM-07). 5. Delete server/services/notify.ts and its re-export at server/services/index.ts:77. It has no callers (`grep -rn notifyOverride` finds only those two lines) and no UI or route, so it is not a user-facing capability. Name sendGenericEmail (emailService.ts:396) as the canonical mail path in the commit message. 6. Add scripts/ci/single-mail-transport.mjs and the npm script ci:single-mail-transport. It fails if any non-test file under server/ other than server/services/emailService.ts imports 'nodemailer' or calls createTransport(. Add it to .husky/pre-push. Run it before step 5 and show it failing on notify.ts, then passing. Add a :selftest that plants a temporary second transport and expects failure. 7. In server/startup/services.ts:284-303 (production only), also require SMTP_FROM's domain to equal MAIL_DOMAIN (a new env var rendered by Terraform from var.mail_domain). When SMTP_HOST matches /^email-smtp\.[a-z0-9-]+\.amazonaws\.com$/, call SESv2 GetEmailIdentity(MAIL_DOMAIN) and require VerifiedForSendingStatus===true and DkimAttributes.Status==='SUCCESS'. On failure, mark the deployment not-ready through server/startup/readiness-state.ts so /readyz reports it, instead of only logging. Grant ses:GetEmailIdentity on that identity to the ECS task role in terraform/modules/ecs-fargate. 8. Founder/ops: after applying, run `node scripts/ops/verify-otp-delivery.mjs` against production with a Gmail inbox, an M365 inbox and, if possible, the pilot customer's domain. Keep the Authentication-Results headers showing spf=pass, dkim=pass and dmarc=pass. Work on concept2cure-v2 only and merge, never rebase.
records.acceptance: a) FAILING FIRST: at HEAD, a production-mode unit test with SMTP_HOST/USER/PASS set and SMTP_FROM unset sees canDeliverLoginCode()===true, so it would send from noreply@concept2cure.pro. After the fix it is false, and POST /api/auth/login answers AUTH_OTP_UNDELIVERABLE. b) `npm run ci:single-mail-transport` fails at HEAD (server/services/notify.ts) and passes after notify.ts is deleted. Its selftest fails on a planted second createTransport. c) `grep -rn "concept2cure\.\(pro\|com\)" server/services/emailService.ts` returns nothing. d) A terraform test run with smtp_from on a domain other than mail_domain fails validation, and terraform plan shows aws_sesv2_email_identity plus outputs for the DKIM CNAMEs, the SPF record and the DMARC record. e) A unit test with a mocked SESv2 client returning DkimAttributes.Status='PENDING' makes readiness report not-ready. f) An OTP received at Gmail and M365 inboxes from production shows spf=pass, dkim=pass and dmarc=pass, recorded by the founder (operational, not code).
records.dependencies: Founder decision on the single domain (also needed by GTM-07 and GTM-19); DNS access for the domain; SES production access in the AWS account; GTM-07 (SUPPORT_EMAIL) for step 4.

records.title: Public self-serve signup is still always on: no kill switch or domain allowlist, column-default limits instead of the free plan, and no AI cost cap
records.evidenceAtHead: `grep -rnE 'SELF_SERVE_SIGNUP|SIGNUP_ENABLED|PUBLIC_SIGNUP|SIGNUP_MODE|ALLOW_SIGNUP|signupEnabled|SIGNUP_DOMAIN|INVITE_ONLY|inviteOnly|DISABLE_SIGNUP' server client/src shared terraform docker-compose*.yml .env.example` finds nothing. server/routes/auth.ts:887 `router.post('/signup', signupLimiter, …)` is open to anyone. The only refusals are no SMTP or no public origin in production (:928-955), the tenant-isolation admission check (assertCanAdmitNewTenant at about :1007, which needs RLS_ENFORCE=on from the second org onward but does not restrict who may sign up), and a duplicate email. auth.ts:1018 inserts the org with only `tier: 'free'`, so the column defaults apply (shared/schema.ts:172-179: seats_purchased 5, max_users 5, max_projects 10, max_storage 5 GB) instead of the published free plan in server/services/billing.ts:104-117 DTC_PRICING (maxUsers 1, maxProjects 2, maxStorageGB 1). provisionLaunchModules then grants the whole launch catalog (auth.ts about :1090-1100). server/services/tenant/tenant-lifecycle.ts:110-118 lists 'incomplete' and 'incomplete_expired' among the allowed payment statuses, with no time limit. AI spend: server/bootstrap/register-ai-routes.ts:19-24 says weekly limits are 'Strictly opt-in per org — with no configured limit the check is a no-op — and fail-open'. Only the 'requests' metric is wired (enforceWeeklyLimit('requests') on /api/ana, /api/ana-ri and /api/chat; public-api.ts:398), and the cost_cents metric (weekly-usage-limits.ts:37) is enforced nowhere. server/services/ai-gateway/policy.ts:420-428 checks only per-request maxTokens. Client: client/src/concept2cure/router/ZenRouter.tsx:210-214 serves /concept2cure/signup, and :230 redirects /signup to it. No commit since 92ccdba1 touches any of this, and no candidate fix exists in `git log 92ccdba1..HEAD --grep`.
records.remaining: 1) There is no way to switch public signup off or limit it to invited orgs or allowlisted domains in production. 2) Self-serve orgs get schema-default limits (5 seats, 5 users, 10 projects, 5 GB) and the full launch catalog instead of the free plan's 1 user, 2 projects and 1 GB. 3) No default AI cost cap is provisioned at org creation, and cost_cents is not enforced on any route or at the gateway. 4) A free or incomplete org is allowed indefinitely. Terms acceptance at signup is tracked separately (GTM-02).
records.severityRationale: The pilot is sales-led on one production AWS environment. While /api/auth/signup stays open, anyone who finds the URL can create a tenant, get the whole launch catalog, upload data under unrecorded terms (GTM-02) and spend model budget without limit. HEAD has mitigations: production signup requires email verification (auth.ts:928-955), a rate limiter, and RLS_ENFORCE=on before a second org can exist. They limit abuse but give no way to close the door, so this must be fixed before pilot users rely on production. Not P0, because it does not break a launch journey or expose another tenant's data.
records.humanTestingNote: Testers will not see this as a defect. Signup works where SMTP and a public origin are configured. A self-signed-up org shows 5 seats and allows 10 projects rather than the published free plan's 1 user and 2 projects, which only shows if someone compares it with the pricing copy. Note for test setup on a deployed environment: a second self-serve org is refused unless RLS_ENFORCE=on (tenant admission). Create tester orgs through the platform-admin path (POST /api/tenants, server/routes/tenants-simple.ts:160) or invite testers into one org.
records.instructions: 1. Founder: confirm whether self-serve is in scope at launch (an audit open question) and set the free-plan AI cost cap (GTM-12). The defaults below work without that decision: off in production, and a conservative cost_cents cap. 2. In server/config (the module that already exports config.billing; add a typed field there), add selfServeSignup: 'off' | 'allowlist' | 'open', read from SELF_SERVE_SIGNUP. It defaults to 'off' when NODE_ENV==='production' and to 'open' otherwise, and an unknown value is treated as 'off'. Also add signupAllowedDomains from SIGNUP_ALLOWED_DOMAINS (comma-separated, lowercased). 3. In server/routes/auth.ts POST /signup (:887), straight after signupSchema.safeParse and before password policy or any DB call, return 403 {success:false, error:{code:'AUTH_SIGNUP_CLOSED', message:'Sign-up is by invitation. Ask your organisation administrator for an invitation.'}} when the mode is 'off', or when it is 'allowlist' and the email's domain is not in signupAllowedDomains. Log one info line without the email address. Invited users are not affected: invitations go through password-setup tokens and POST /api/tenant-users/invitations/:invitationId/accept (server/routes/tenant-users.ts:202), not /signup (see the emailService.ts:425-435 note). Sales-led tenants are created through POST /api/tenants (server/routes/tenants-simple.ts:160, requirePlatformAdmin). 4. Add GET /api/auth/signup-availability, public and data-free, returning {mode:'off'|'allowlist'|'open'}. In client/src/concept2cure/auth/ZenSignup.tsx, call it on mount and render an honest 'Sign-up is by invitation' state with a link back to login when the mode is 'off'. Also handle AUTH_SIGNUP_CLOSED from the POST. Hide any 'Create account' link on the login page when the mode is 'off'. Keep the /concept2cure/signup route (ZenRouter.tsx:210-214) so no capability is deleted. 5. Terraform: add variable self_serve_signup (default "off", validation on the three values) and signup_allowed_domains (default "") to terraform/stack/variables.tf, and render them in the env list in terraform/stack/main.tf next to SMTP_FROM (about :288). Add them to docker-compose.yml and docker-compose.beta.yml. 6. Apply plan limits at creation. Next to DTC_PRICING in server/services/billing.ts:104, export limitsForTier(tier), which returns {seatsPurchased, maxUsers, maxProjects, maxStorage} from that table. Use it in the signup insert at auth.ts:1018 (`.values({ …, tier: 'free', ...limitsForTier('free') })`) and in the org insert in server/routes/tenants-simple.ts POST / (honouring an explicit platform-admin override). Do NOT change the shared/schema.ts:172-179 column defaults. If the defaults must change, amend the migration that creates them in place, with a dated header note (CLAUDE.md Rule 1). 7. Default AI cost cap: inside the runWithTenantScope block after provisionLaunchModules (auth.ts about :1090-1100), call setWeeklyLimit(result.org.id, {metric:'cost_cents', weeklyLimit:<free cap>, overageCapPct:0, overageHardCap:null, warnThresholdPct:80, weekStartDow:1, enabled:true}, {userId: result.user.id}, 'Plan default at provisioning: free') from server/services/weekly-usage-limits.ts:278. Do the same in tenants-simple.ts with the plan the operator picks. 8. Enforce cost at the single choke point: in server/services/ai-gateway/gateway.ts, just before or after this.policyEngine.evaluate(request) (:1418) and before the provider call, call checkWeeklyLimit(orgId, 'cost_cents', 0). If decision.allowed===false, refuse with a typed USAGE_LIMIT_REACHED error that routes map to 429, and audit the refusal. This covers every AI route, not only /api/ana, /api/ana-ri and /api/chat. Keep the existing fail-open behaviour on a metering outage, but raise reportSecurityAlert so it is visible. 9. Verify every gate by making it fail first: write the tests in Acceptance against HEAD, show them failing, then implement. Work on concept2cure-v2 only and merge, never rebase.
records.acceptance: a) FAILING FIRST: a route test with NODE_ENV=production and SELF_SERVE_SIGNUP unset POSTs a valid body to /api/auth/signup. At HEAD it gets past validation (201, or 503 when SMTP is mocked off). After the fix it gets 403 AUTH_SIGNUP_CLOSED, and no organizations insert is attempted. b) With SELF_SERVE_SIGNUP=allowlist and SIGNUP_ALLOWED_DOMAINS=acme.com, a@acme.com proceeds and a@other.com gets 403. c) With signup off, POST /api/tenant-users/invitations/:id/accept and platform-admin POST /api/tenants still succeed. d) tests/db/signup-launch-catalog.dbtest.ts is extended: a self-serve org has seats_purchased=1, max_users=1, max_projects=2, max_storage=1, and has a weekly_usage_limits row with metric='cost_cents' and enabled=true. This fails at HEAD (5/5/10/5 and no row). e) A gateway unit test: an org whose api_usage_logs cost_cents for the week is at or above its cap gets USAGE_LIMIT_REACHED on a non-chat AI call, and the provider mock is never invoked. f) In the Terraform test, self_serve_signup defaults to "off" and the rendered task definition contains SELF_SERVE_SIGNUP=off. g) A ZenSignup component test renders the invitation-only state when signup-availability returns 'off'.
records.dependencies: Founder: whether self-serve exists at launch, and the free-plan cost cap (GTM-12). GTM-02 (record terms acceptance) applies whenever signup is set to 'open' or 'allowlist'. GTM-08 (seat self-grant) is closed in the same work order (WO-D).

records.title: There is still no human support channel. 'Get help' opens AnA, the support mailbox is a placeholder, and the security contact switches between .pro and .com
records.evidenceAtHead: client/src/concept2cure/v2/Shell.tsx:74-76 still has `const HELP_SURFACE = 'conversation-thread'` (AnA). In the account menu at :375-376, 'Codebase coverage' is followed by 'Get help' pointing to HELP_SURFACE, and the header help button at :599-608 calls onNav(HELP_SURFACE). The menu click handler at :457-460 knows only 'logout', 'account' and `to`. `grep -rniE 'contact support|mailto:support|support@|SUPPORT_EMAIL|supportEmail|report a problem' client/src` finds nothing. On the server, the only hits are the email template text 'support@concept2cure.com' (server/services/emailService.ts:243) and 'Quote the reference below if you contact support.' (server/lib/api-response.ts:165), which names no channel. The X-Request-Id support handle in client/src/concept2cure/v2/dataConnect.tsx:509-540 already existed at 92ccdba1. docs/commercial/SUPPORT_POLICY.md:28 still says 'support@[domain]', and the Sev-1 founder mobile at :30 is a placeholder. The security contact is security@concept2cure.pro in SUPPORT_POLICY.md:31, SECURITY.md:17,150 and the server/routes/well-known.ts:16 default, but security@concept2cure.com and support@concept2cure.com '(to be confirmed)' in docs/connector/SUPPORT.md:3,13. Terraform renders no SUPPORT_EMAIL or SECURITY_CONTACT_EMAIL (grep terraform/ is empty). `git log 92ccdba1..HEAD --grep` finds no support-channel commit.
records.remaining: 1) No live, named support mailbox or ticket tool, and no Sev-1 contact; this is founder work. 2) No 'Contact support' entry in the product that sends a pre-filled context block (org, user, surface, request ID, time). 3) There is no single domain: the security contact is .pro in code and SECURITY.md and .com in the connector docs, and support is .com in an email template but a placeholder in the policy. 4) SUPPORT_EMAIL and SECURITY_CONTACT_EMAIL are not deployment config, so well-known.ts falls back to a hard-coded .pro address.
records.severityRationale: During a pilot, users must be able to raise a Sev-1 (including 'nobody can log in', see GTM-05) and know where security reports go. Today the product only offers an AI chat, and the policy the customer would sign names a mailbox that does not exist. A founder-supported pilot can partly cover this with a Slack Connect channel set up at onboarding, so it is not P0. But the mailbox, the domain and an in-product route are needed before pilot users rely on production.
records.humanTestingNote: A tester who hits a problem and clicks 'Get help' (account menu or header) gets an AnA conversation, not a person or a ticket form, and the product has no other way to report a bug. Error panels show a request reference to quote, but say nowhere where to quote it. Workaround: give testers an out-of-band channel (the test team's Slack or issue tracker) and ask them to paste the request reference from the error panel, the page URL and the time.
records.instructions: 1. Founder: decide the single domain (shared with GTM-05). Create the support@ and security@ mailboxes on it, plus a ticketing or shared-inbox tool, and name the Sev-1 contact. Fill the placeholders at docs/commercial/SUPPORT_POLICY.md:28-31 and make docs/connector/SUPPORT.md:3,13 and SECURITY.md:17,150 name the same addresses. 2. Terraform: add variables support_email and security_contact_email to terraform/stack/variables.tf. Make them required (no default) with the same email regex used by smtp_from (:292-299), and render SUPPORT_EMAIL and SECURITY_CONTACT_EMAIL in the env list in terraform/stack/main.tf next to SMTP_FROM (about :288). Add both to docker-compose.yml and docker-compose.beta.yml with `${VAR:?…}`. Add a tftest run that omits support_email and expects plan failure. 3. server/routes/well-known.ts:16: remove the 'security@concept2cure.pro' fallback. If SECURITY_CONTACT_EMAIL is unset in production, /.well-known/security.txt returns 404 and boot logs a CRITICAL line, which fails closed rather than publishing a possibly wrong address. Outside production, keep a clearly fake dev value. 4. server/services/emailService.ts:243: replace 'support@concept2cure.com' with process.env.SUPPORT_EMAIL, and leave the sentence out when it is unset. 5. Expose the address to the signed-in client: add supportEmail (string|null) to the GET /api/auth/me payload (server/routes/auth.ts:1631) or the GET /api/auth/session payload (:258), read from process.env.SUPPORT_EMAIL. 6. In client/src/concept2cure/v2/Shell.tsx, add an account-menu item next to 'Get help' (:376): `{ label: 'Contact support', ic: 'mail', action: 'contact-support' }`. The 'mail' icon exists at client/src/concept2cure/v2/icons.tsx:259. Handle it in the click handler at :457-460 by opening `mailto:${supportEmail}?subject=…&body=…`. The body is pre-filled with organisation name and id, user email, current surface or route, the last X-Request-Id seen by dataConnect.tsx (expose it from the existing support-handle state), UTC timestamp and app build id. When supportEmail is null, show the item disabled with the text 'Support contact not configured for this deployment' rather than hiding the problem. Keep 'Get help' pointing to AnA; this adds a human channel and replaces nothing. 7. On the error panel in dataConnect.tsx (:509-540), add a 'Contact support' link that uses the same mailto builder and includes that error's request ID. 8. Tests (fail first): a Shell test asserting the account menu contains a 'Contact support' item whose href or handler targets mailto: with the request ID in the body (fails at HEAD), and a well-known test asserting no hard-coded .pro fallback (fails at HEAD). Work on concept2cure-v2 only and merge, never rebase.
records.acceptance: a) FAILING FIRST: a new client test (client/src/concept2cure/v2/__tests__/) renders the account menu with supportEmail='support@example.test'. It expects a 'Contact support' menuitem whose activation builds a mailto: URL containing the org id, the surface and the last request ID. It fails at HEAD. b) With supportEmail=null, the item renders disabled with the 'not configured' text. c) A server test: with NODE_ENV=production and SECURITY_CONTACT_EMAIL unset, GET /.well-known/security.txt returns 404, and `grep -n "concept2cure\.pro" server/routes/well-known.ts` returns nothing. d) A terraform test: plan without support_email fails, and the rendered task definition contains SUPPORT_EMAIL and SECURITY_CONTACT_EMAIL. e) `grep -rn "support@\[domain\]\|to be confirmed" docs/commercial/SUPPORT_POLICY.md docs/connector/SUPPORT.md` returns nothing, and every support and security address across SECURITY.md, docs/commercial and docs/connector uses one domain. f) Operational: a test email to support@ and security@ creates a ticket or inbox item (founder).
records.dependencies: Founder: domain decision, mailbox and ticket-tool setup, and Sev-1 contact (shared with GTM-05 and GTM-19). GTM-05 step 4 uses the same SUPPORT_EMAIL variable.
